lesson: Listen to where it starts, not with you, not with a thought, but with a gate, half-latched, still swinging from a hand that already left. That's a choice. It drops us into a chore mid-motion, and right away the world's a little unfinished, a little on you. Watch how the images pass the work along, one to the next. The loose hinge becomes the jobs waiting with their mouths open, which becomes the fog that won't decide, the swollen barn door needing a shoulder. Each picture hands you a small weight to carry, same as that list, with your name pressed in. Then the turn. None of it moves without you. That's where the fence and fog stop being scenery, and become the plain fact of a life. You're the hands the day is waiting on. Here's the one to steal. Let an ordinary object carry the whole feeling before you ever name it. I'll let you hear it now.
